_comment: Captured shape of mcp.calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource as of 2026-04-30. Paired with the SKILL.md empirical-verification timestamp. If the consent screen scope-count, permission labels, or OAuth metadata fields drift, an outsider can compare a fresh fetch against this snapshot to localise the change without needing a live test harness.

drift_check_recipe.step_1: From any shell with curl: curl -s https://mcp.calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource | jq '.'
drift_check_recipe.step_2: Compare the live response's scopes_supported array against the array above. A new entry probably means a new tool category is available. A removed entry means a tool was retired and a SKILL Tool Reference row needs updating.
drift_check_recipe.step_3: If the scopes_supported list is byte-identical to this snapshot, no SKILL changes needed. If different, open an issue and update the SKILL.md Phase 2 Tool Reference to match before re-running Phase 1.
drift_check_recipe.step_4_in_session_guard: The SKILL also runs an in-session tool-name-drift guard before the first Phase 2 call (see SKILL.md Phase 2 introduction). The guard lists available mcp__calendly__* tools and flags any canonical name that has disappeared. Run that on a live session for a faster signal than diffing the well-known endpoint.
drift_check_recipe.out_of_band_signal: If Calendly ships a new consent screen design with different permission labels or count, the worked example transcript at examples/calendly-meetings-list-session.md is the first place a non-technical user notices because the narration line in Step 4a paraphrases the consent text. Update both the SKILL and the example together.

_why_no_automated_script: An automated drift-check script would belong in tests/ and this connector lives inside the larger claude-workshop-kit repo where tests/ is reserved for the kit-wide smoke and verification harness. Drift checking on a third-party SaaS is also rate-limit-aware work; it should run from a human or a scheduled job, not from every PR's CI run. The snapshot here is the durable artifact; the script is left as a one-line curl in drift_check_recipe.step_1.
